options.text: Gas particles colliding with the walls of their container
Gas particles being packed closely together

questions.explanation: Gas pressure is caused by gas particles moving randomly at high speeds and colliding with the walls of their container. Each collision exerts a small force on the wall, and the combined effect of billions of collisions per second creates pressure.

questions.stem: If the temperature of a gas in a sealed container increases (at constant volume), the pressure increases because:

options.text: The particles move faster and collide with the walls more frequently and with greater force

questions.explanation: At higher temperatures, gas particles have more kinetic energy and move faster. They collide with the container walls more frequently and with greater force, which increases the pressure.
